mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p1.title: Look at the last digit
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p1.body:
A whole number is a multiple of 5 exactly when its last digit is 0 or 5. Only 55 ends in 5.

**Answer: (E) 55**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p1.title: Count in fives
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p1.body:
Counting in fives: 45, 50, 55, 60. Of the five numbers, only 55 is on this list.

**Answer: (E) 55**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p2.title: Count the triangles
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p2.body:
The hexagon is split into 6 equal triangles and 2 of them are shaded. So the shaded fraction is $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{1}{3}$**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p2.title: Pair them up
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-p2.body:
Group the 6 triangles into 3 pairs. The 2 shaded triangles make one pair out of 3, which is $\frac{1}{3}$.

**Answer: (A) $\frac{1}{3}$**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-01.title: Add the two groups
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-01.body:
- Three children with 4 balloons each: $3 \times 4 = 12$.
- Four children with 3 balloons each: $4 \times 3 = 12$.
- Altogether $12 + 12 = 24$.

**Answer: (D) 24**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-01.title: Notice they are the same
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-01.body:
$3 \times 4$ and $4 \times 3$ are the same number, 12. So the total is $2 \times 12 = 24$.

**Answer: (D) 24**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-02.title: Convert kilograms to grams
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-02.body:
The label says 0.4 kg. There are 1000 grams in a kilogram, so $0.4 \times 1000 = 400$ grams.

**Answer: (D) 400 grams**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-02.title: Use a fraction
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-02.body:
$0.4$ kg is $\frac{4}{10}$ of a kilogram. One tenth of 1000 g is 100 g, so four tenths is 400 g.

**Answer: (D) 400 grams**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-03.title: Check each word
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-03.body:
A letter has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after turning it upside down (half a turn). The capital letters that do are H, I, N, O, S, X and Z.
- BISON has B, DOZEN has D and E, SAXON has A, CHINO has C — these letters do not.
- ONION uses only O, N and I, which all do.

**Answer: (A) ONION**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-03.title: Spot the bad letters
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-03.body:
Turn each word upside down in your head. B, D, E, A and C all change when turned half a turn, which rules out every word except ONION.

**Answer: (A) ONION**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-04.title: Count on
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-04.body:
From 1028 to 2028 is 1000 years, but 2018 is 10 years before 2028, so it is $1000 - 10 = 990$ years.

**Answer: (D) 990**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-05.title: Change to centimetres
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-05.body:
$201.8$ mm $= 20.18$ cm, about 20 cm.
- A big toe is only a few cm long.
- A door is about 200 cm high, a stadium hundreds of metres across, and a galaxy unimaginably wide.
- The paper was A4, which is about 21 cm wide.

**Answer: (B) the width of a page of the question paper**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-05.title: Think of a ruler
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-05.body:
201.8 mm is a little less than the length of a 30 cm school ruler — about two thirds of it. Only the width of a sheet of paper is anywhere near that.

**Answer: (B) the width of a page of the question paper**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-06.title: Add up each part
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-06.body:
The graph shows the distance from home. Follow the line:
- 800 m down to 600 m: 200 m
- back up to 800 m: 200 m
- down to 200 m: 600 m
- back up to 400 m: 200 m
- (flat part: reading, no walking)
- down to 0 m: 400 m

Total: $200 + 200 + 600 + 200 + 400 = 1600$ m.

**Answer: (E) 1600 m**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-06.title: Extra walking
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-06.body:
Going straight home would be 800 m. Twice he walked 200 m back the wrong way and then had to walk those 200 m again. That adds $2 \times 2 \times 200 = 800$ m, so the total is $800 + 800 = 1600$ m.

**Answer: (E) 1600 m**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-07.title: Total the minutes
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-07.body:
$45 + 3 + 15 + 45 + 3 = 111$ minutes, which is 1 hour 51 minutes. 7.45 p.m. plus 1 hour is 8.45 p.m., plus 51 minutes is 9.36 p.m.

**Answer: (E) 9.36 p.m.**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-07.title: Step through the match
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-07.body:
- First half with extra time: 7.45 + 48 min = 8.33 p.m.
- Half-time: 8.33 + 15 min = 8.48 p.m.
- Second half with extra time: 8.48 + 48 min = 9.36 p.m.

**Answer: (E) 9.36 p.m.**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-08.title: Estimate
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-08.body:
20.18 is a lot smaller than 50.45, a bit less than half of it. Multiplying by 0.4 (which is $\frac{2}{5}$) takes a bit less than half, and $\frac{2}{5}$ of 50 is 20.

**Answer: (C) pressing × instead of −**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-09.title: Compare with the odd numbers
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-09.body:
The even numbers 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 are each 1 more than the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. So their sum is $25 + 5 \times 1 = 30$.

**Answer: (A) 30**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-10.title: Count the numbers with a 4
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-10.body:
Numbers with a 4 in the units place: 4, 14, 24, 34, 44, 54, 64, 74, 84, 94 (10 numbers). Numbers 40–49 have a 4 in the tens place: 10 more, but 44 was already counted. So $10 + 10 - 1 = 19$ numbers contain a 4, and $100 - 19 = 81$ are left.

**Answer: (D) 81**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-10.title: Count the good numbers directly
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-10.body:
Think of 0 to 99 as two-digit numbers 00–99. Each digit can be any of the 9 digits other than 4, giving $9 \times 9 = 81$ numbers. This includes 00 but not 100; 00 is not a house and 100 is a fine house, so the count stays 81.

**Answer: (D) 81**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-11.title: Stand on the right
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-11.body:
Picture standing at arrow (C) and looking at the block. The back of the block is then on your right-hand side. The part of the block that is two cubes high is at the back, so you see a row of three squares with one extra square on top at the right-hand end — exactly the view shown.

**Answer: (C) from the right**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-11.title: Rule the others out
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-11.body:
- From above you see only the top outline of the block, with no heights at all.
- From the front or the back you look across the block's width, and the raised part looks two cubes wide, not one.
- The view from the left is the mirror image of the view from the right, so it has the extra square on the left-hand end; the given view has it on the right.

Only the view from the right is left.

**Answer: (C) from the right**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-12.title: Use 10%
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-12.body:
10% of three million is 300 000. Six hundred thousand is twice that, so it is 20%.

**Answer: (B) 20%**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-13.title: Use both facts about Mo
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-13.body:
Mo's amount is made of £5 notes, so it is a multiple of 5; it is also a multiple of 13. So it is a multiple of $5 \times 13 = 65$. The only such amount up to £100 (that is not £0) is £65, so Jo got $100 - 65 = 35$ pounds.

**Answer: (C) £35**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-13.title: List multiples of 13
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-13.body:
Multiples of 13 up to 100: 13, 26, 39, 52, 65, 78, 91. Only 65 ends in 0 or 5, so only it can be made from £5 notes. Jo has £35.

**Answer: (C) £35**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-14.title: Fingers per brick
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-14.body:
Each brick gives $6 \times 4 = 24$ fingers, and 4 bricks give $4 \times 24 = 96$.

**Answer: (E) 96**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-15.title: Take away the bites
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-15.body:
The toast has area $12 \times 12 = 144$ cm². Each bite is $3 \times 3 = 9$ cm², so four bites remove $36$ cm². Left: $144 - 36 = 108$ cm².

**Answer: (B) 108 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-15.title: Count 3 cm squares
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-15.body:
Split the toast into 3 cm squares: it is 4 by 4, so 16 squares. Four squares are bitten out, leaving 12 squares of 9 cm² each: $12 \times 9 = 108$ cm².

**Answer: (B) 108 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-16.title: Find the extra cake
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-16.body:
Freddy's order is Teddy's order plus one extra cake, so a cake costs $£6.25 - £3.75 = £2.50$. Then the coffee costs $£3.75 - £2.50 = £1.25$.

**Answer: (B) £1.25**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-16.title: Check the options
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-16.body:
If the coffee is £1.25, then the cake is £2.50, and coffee plus 2 cakes is $1.25 + 5.00 = £6.25$. ✓

**Answer: (B) £1.25**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-17.title: Count from each corner
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-17.body:
From each of the 6 corners you can draw a diagonal to every corner except itself and its two neighbours: 3 diagonals. That is $6 \times 3 = 18$, but each diagonal has been counted from both ends, so there are $18 \div 2 = 9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-17.title: Lines minus sides
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-17.body:
Any two of the 6 corners can be joined by a line: $\frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15$ lines. Six of these are sides, so $15 - 6 = 9$ are diagonals.

**Answer: (B) 9**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-18.title: Number the days
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-18.body:
Call 12 November day 0. Dad changes on days 0, 2, 4, …; Tammy on 0, 3, 6, …; so both on multiples of 6: days 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, … Wednesday 14 November is day 2, and Wednesdays are days 2, 9, 16, 23, 30, … The first day on both lists is day 30. November has 30 days, so day 30 is 12 December.

**Answer: (E) 12 December**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-18.title: Check the dates
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-18.body:
Dad and Tammy change together every 6 days: 18 Nov (Sun), 24 Nov (Sat), 30 Nov (Fri), 6 Dec (Thu), 12 Dec (Wed). The first of these that is a Wednesday is 12 December.

**Answer: (E) 12 December**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-19.title: Angles on a straight line
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-19.body:
At each of the three points where the square touches the triangle, the two shaded angles and the square's right angle make a straight line, 180°. So each pair of shaded angles adds to $180° - 90° = 90°$. Three pairs: $3 \times 90° = 270°$.

**Answer: (D) 270°**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-19.title: Total along the sides
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-19.body:
Along each of the three sides, at the touching point the angles make a straight line: $3 \times 180° = 540°$ in total. The square's three corners that touch the sides take $3 \times 90° = 270°$ of this. The shaded angles are the rest: $540° - 270° = 270°$.

**Answer: (D) 270°**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-20.title: Make a table
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-20.body:
Pages left after each part of the day:
- Day 1: morning $444 - 20 = 424$, evening $424 - 212 = 212$
- Day 2: $212 - 20 = 192$, then $96$
- Day 3: $96 - 20 = 76$, then $38$
- Day 4: $38 - 20 = 18$, then $9$
- Day 5: she reads the last 9 pages in the morning.

**Answer: (C) 5 days**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-20.title: Work backwards
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-20.body:
She finishes on a morning when 20 or fewer pages are left. At the start of a day, the pages left go 444, 212, 96, 38, 9. On the fifth day only 9 pages remain, which she reads that morning.

**Answer: (C) 5 days**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-21.title: Think in fifths
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-21.body:
Dividing by 5 gives one fifth of the number. Adding 20 brings it back up to the whole number, so 20 must be the other four fifths. One fifth is $20 \div 4 = 5$, so the number is $5 \times 5 = 25$.

**Answer: 25**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-21.title: Try and check
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-21.body:
Try 25: $25 \div 5 = 5$, $5 + 20 = 25$ ✓. (Try 20: $4 + 20 = 24$, too big; try 30: $6 + 20 = 26$, too small — the answer is in between and 25 works.)

**Answer: 25**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-22.title: Find the side lengths
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-22.body:
- Bedroom: $18 = 6 \times 3$ with length twice the width, so 6 m long and 3 m wide.
- Living room: $32 = 8 \times 4$, so 8 m long and 4 m wide.
- The study shares the 4 m height of the living room: $20 \div 4 = 5$ m long.
- So the house is $8 + 5 = 13$ m long. The top row is 3 m tall (the bedroom's width), and the bedroom takes 6 m of it.
- Kitchen: $(13 - 6) \times 3 = 7 \times 3 = 21$ m².

**Answer: 21 m²**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-22.title: Whole house minus rooms
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-22.body:
From the side lengths above the house is 13 m long and $3 + 4 = 7$ m high, so its area is $13 \times 7 = 91$ m². The kitchen is what is left: $91 - 18 - 32 - 20 = 21$ m².

**Answer: 21 m²**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-23.title: Build it from the outside in
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-23.body:
A six-digit palindrome looks like $ABCCBA$.
- A multiple of 6 is even, so the last digit $A$ is even. Make it as big as possible: $A = 8$.
- Next make $B = 9$.
- It must also be a multiple of 3, so the digit sum $8+9+C+C+9+8 = 34 + 2C$ must be a multiple of 3. $C = 9$: 52 no; $C = 8$: 50 no; $C = 7$: 48 yes.

So the number is 897798.

**Answer: 897798**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-23.title: Check downward
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-23.body:
Palindromes starting with 9 end in 9 and are odd, so none work. Start from 899998 and go down through 89BCCB98-type numbers: 899998 (digit sum 52), 898898 (50), 897798 (48 ✓). $897798 \div 6 = 149633$.

**Answer: 897798**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-24.title: Use ratios
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-24.body:
Cars : bikes $= 4 : 3$ and bikes : lorries $= 5 : 4$. Make the bikes match: cars : bikes $= 20 : 15$ and bikes : lorries $= 15 : 12$, so cars : bikes : lorries $= 20 : 15 : 12$. The total is a multiple of $20 + 15 + 12 = 47$. Even and less than 100 means $2 \times 47 = 94$.

**Answer: 94** (40 cars, 30 bikes and 24 lorries)

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-24.title: Start from the lorries
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-24.body:
The lorries must split into quarters, so try multiples of 4. With 12 lorries: bikes $12 + 3 = 15$, cars $15 + 5 = 20$, total 47 (odd). With 24 lorries: 30 bikes, 40 cars, total 94 — even and less than 100. With 36 lorries the total would be 141, too many.

**Answer: 94**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-25.title: Look at the gaps
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-25.body:
Going round the table, the 5 friends without poppers are split into 3 gaps between the poppers, each gap at least 1. The gaps can be $1, 1, 3$ or $1, 2, 2$ (in some order around the table). Each pattern can be turned round the table into 8 different positions, and no position is repeated. So there are $2 \times 8 = 16$ ways.

**Answer: 16**

mapmc-pmc-2018-11-25.title: Count systematically
mapmc-pmc-2018-11-25.body:
Number the seats 1 to 8. Count the choices that include seat 1: then seats 2 and 8 are out, and we choose 2 non-neighbouring seats from 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (in a row): $\{3,5\},\{3,6\},\{3,7\},\{4,6\},\{4,7\},\{5,7\}$, which is 6 ways. Each seat is in 6 choices, giving $8 \times 6 = 48$, but each choice has 3 seats and was counted 3 times: $48 \div 3 = 16$.

**Answer: 16**
